To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of heterogeneous distributed systems can be significantly improved by considering both system heterogeneity in computing power and memory resources.
the performance of load sharing policies in distributed systems is robust against the variation of memory demand distributions of workload and the variation of system heterogeneity.
the performance of load sharing policies considering memory resources in heterogeneous distributed systems are robust and independent of the distribution of memory demand of workloads.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of load balancing policies which can effectively share CPU and memory resources in heterogeneous distributed systems.
the following questions: How to design load sharing policies for distributed systems with heterogeneous workstations?
the following issues: (1) How to design effective load sharing policies in heterogeneous distributed environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

load sharing policies should be designed with both system heterogeneity in mind as well as effective use of memory resources in order to achieve the best overall performance in distributed computing environments.
the load sharing policies considering memory resources and system heterogeneity are effective in heterogeneous distributed environments.

, for heterogeneous distributed environments with a large variation of computing power and memory capacity, the performance of a load sharing policy is not determined solely by the CPU load of the system, but also by the memory demand of the workloads.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

load sharing on distributed systems can be made effective in both homogeneous and heterogeneous environments, and that the performance of load sharing policies is quite robust to the variation of memory demand distributions of the workloads.

, for the purpose of minimizing both CPU idle times as well as the number of page-faults, a load sharing policy considering both memory and computing resources can be effective in heterogeneous networks of work-stations.
load sharing policies which consider both CPU and memory resource usages in heterogeneous systems, are more efficient and more robust than policies which only consider the CPU resources.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of load sharing policies is more sensitive to the distribution of the computing power of workstations than to the distribution of memory capacities.

the design and implementation of load sharing policies should be done with considerations on the heterogeneity of the systems, the memory resources of the workstations, and the memory demand distribution of the workloads.
load sharing policies which consider memory resources can be effective in heterogeneous distributed systems, and the design of such load sharing policies is not dependent on the nature of workloads.
